siteTitle: The Current War: Film Review & Historical Analysis

sections.heading: Overview & Core Thesis
sections.summary: An examination of Alfonso Gomez-Rejon's 'The Current War', focusing on the battle between Edison's DC infrastructure and Westinghouse-Tesla's AC polyphase grid.
sections.callout: Film Rating: Historical Fidelity vs. Dramatic Tension

sections.heading: The Physics & Economics: AC vs. DC
sections.summary: Edison's direct current grid hit severe copper-gauge and line-loss limitations over distance, requiring generation plants every mile. Westinghouse capitalized on alternating current and transformers to step up voltage for long-distance, low-loss transmission.
techDetails: DC Constraints: Low voltage, high current, heavy I²R thermal losses.
AC Advantage: High-voltage step-up reduces current and conductor mass.
The Chicago World's Fair (1893): Westinghouse severely underbids General Electric.

sections.heading: Key Scene: The World's Columbian Exposition
sections.commentary: Analysis of the lighting of the 1893 fair and the visual contrast between Edison's personal brand and Westinghouse's industrial execution.
